text:
deploy-bot: Rollout finished for inference-edge:v2026-03-14-12 (canary 10%) at 04:05 UTC
deploy-bot: Steps: build->push->deploy. Tag: v2026-03-14-12. :white_check_mark:
observability-bot: Alert rule triggered: 503_rate > 3% over 1m on /v1/generate (service=inference-edge)
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident PDI-85912 triggered by alert '503 spike - inference-edge'
pagerduty-bot: Severity: high. Symptoms: increased 5xx ratio (503), error bursts affecting throughput. Impact: some requests retry/fail.
alice (oncall): ping — I see the PD page. grabbing logs now.
alice (oncall): how widespread? any customer-facing errors reported?
luca (product-support): seeing ~20 support tickets opening in last 8m, several mention failures in generation and retries causing UI errors. not wide but real customers impacted.
sanjay (eng-sre): joining. can you paste the PD details?
pagerduty-bot: Incident PDI-85912 | Trigger: infra.observability.rule.503_spike | Affected hosts: edge-7, edge-11, edge-13 (canary pool), rate=6.7%
marie (eng-runtime): interesting — canary nodes only in pool 'canary-us-west-2' per rollout config. sounds like the new model or runtime change is hitting the canary.
alice (oncall): logs from edge-11 show repeated: `ModelExecutionError: KV cache miss during warmup` then `upstream timeout` spikes.
sanjay (eng-sre): paste sample logs?
alice (oncall): ```
[04:09:12] request_id=abc123 model=inference-x qlen=512 stage=kv_load error="KV cache miss"
[04:09:12] request_id=abc124 upstream_error="rpc timeout"
```
marie (eng-runtime): that KV cache miss pattern matches the new runtime patch we rolled that changes on-demand cache population for sharded models. could be a race under the specific request mix.
luca (product-support): hold on — tickets show elevated latency then 503s. not yet a major outage, but users hitting interactive flows see failures.
sanjay (eng-sre): we should divert canary traffic immediately and sos-check fallback policy. two options: 1) pause/scale-down canary or 2) route traffic off canary to previous stable variant. which is faster?
marie (eng-runtime): routing off canary is fastest and non-destructive. I can flip traffic weights.
alice (oncall): I'll ack the PD and mark next steps. `pdbot ack PDI-85912 — alice`
pagerduty-bot: PDI-85912 acknowledged by alice (oncall) at 04:11 UTC
sanjay (eng-sre): marie, please execute traffic divert. share command so I can monitor.
marie (eng-runtime): running: ```
# route 100% traffic back to inference-edge:v2026-03-14-11 (stable)
redwoodctl rollout traffic-set --service inference-edge --from v2026-03-14-12 --to v2026-03-14-11 --percent 100
```
marie (eng-runtime): done. waiting for propagation (CDN & routing caches TTL ~10s).
observability-bot: Traffic shift applied. Canary weight -> 0%.
observability-bot: 503_rate dropping: 6.7% -> 0.4% over 30s window.
luca (product-support): tickets are calming. some retries succeeded.
alice (oncall): good. is rollback required or canary debug first?
sanjay (eng-sre): we need rapid root cause. but since user impact reduced, do a canary rollback to be safe. marie can you initiate rollback of v2026-03-14-12 from canary hosts?
marie (eng-runtime): initiating rollback to v2026-03-14-11 on canary nodes now. command: ```
redwoodctl rollout rollback --service inference-edge --revision v2026-03-14-12 --target canary-us-west-2 --confirm
```
deploy-bot: Rollback job started (job id rb-20260314-0901). Estimated completion: 2m.
alice (oncall): I'll update PD incident status: 'mitigated - traffic diverted and rollback in progress'
pagerduty-bot: PDI-85912 status updated: mitigated (acknowledged) by alice
sanjay (eng-sre): monitoring logs and kv cache metrics. looking for degraded latencies or error traces after rollback.
marie (eng-runtime): rollback completed on canary hosts. verify: all canary pods now on v2026-03-14-11
observability-bot: Post-rollback 503_rate steady at 0.2%. latency normalized to baseline.
luca (product-support): customers reporting recovered. closing urgent tickets.
alice (oncall): I'll close the PD once we confirm stability for 15m. anyone object to declaring incident resolved if metrics hold?
sanjay (eng-sre): no objection. we should capture RCA: regression introduced by cache-on-demand race in runtime patch. assign to marie + runtime team to run a repro and fix. also need to check canary gating (we saw full canary failure threshold not blocking traffic quick enough).
marie (eng-runtime): will file an action ticket and start a bisect on the runtime commit range. I'll include reproducer and mitigation (force synchronous cache warmup for sharded models).
alice (oncall): final notes I'll put in the PD incident summary: - cause: runtime KV cache race on new patch - impact: ~6% 503s on canary hosts, small number of customer-facing failures, mitigated by traffic diversion and rollback - mitigation: diverted traffic, rolled back canary - owner: marie (eng-runtime) - follow-ups: fix runtime, improve canary gating thresholds, add synthetic tests for cache consistency
pagerduty-bot: PDI-85912 marked resolved by alice at 04:21 UTC
alice (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll create a short postmortem outline and tag runtime + srep for next steps. :thumbsup: 
sanjay (eng-sre): quick wins: tighten canary abort threshold to 3% 5xx in 30s and auto-route fallback. We'll propose in the postmortem.
luca (product-support): will send a short customer comms template for any affected users.
marie (eng-runtime): starting bisect now. logging progress in #eng-runtime and will link the PR.
alice (oncall): closing thread. follow-ups tracked in RED-issue-583 (postmortem)
